commenter_information.credentials_or_expertise_mentioned: Event notification and care coordination technology vendor that routes alerts to authorized recipients using hospital event messages, attribution/roster matching, and workflow-triggered notification delivery.

executive_summary: Bamboo Health supports expanding electronic event notifications but urges CMS to preserve HL7 v2 ADT as the current production-ready real-time push standard while piloting FHIR approaches. It recommends a tiered data model, stronger patient matching and attribution, provider directory modernization, permissible sharing guidance for behavioral health data, and TEFCA evolution toward operational real-time push workflows.

regulatory_citations_mentioned: 2020 CMS Interoperability and Patient Access final rule event notification requirements
standards_referenced: HL7 Da Vinci Unsolicited Notifications IG
HL7 Da Vinci Member Attribution List IG

detailed_positions.topic: Preserve HL7 v2 ADT while modernizing
detailed_positions.rationale: HL7 v2 ADT is widely deployed, real-time, push-based, and production-ready; FHIR push notifications are not yet mature or uniformly deployed.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Maintain HL7 v2 ADT as the operational backbone while piloting FHIR Subscriptions and Da Vinci Unsolicited Notifications in targeted use cases.

detailed_positions.rationale: Additional data can improve routing and actionability but overloading notifications could degrade real-time performance and burden hospitals.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Use a tiered model with limited minimum fields and enhanced profiles for care management, transitions, behavioral health follow-up, and value-based workflows where available and lawful.

detailed_positions.rationale: TEFCA may expand reach and reduce duplicative agreements but is currently primarily query-based and lacks standardized real-time push infrastructure.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Develop a TEFCA use case for real-time push-based event notifications covering routing, authorization, endpoint discovery, patient matching, delivery confirmation, and technical routing entities.

detailed_positions.rationale: State law and 42 CFR Part 2 fragmentation leads to over-redaction or suppression of behavioral health event data.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Provide federal guidance on permissible encounter-level sharing and adopt tiered data segmentation to allow basic event notifications while protecting sensitive details.

detailed_positions.rationale: Notification value depends on routing to the right authorized recipient; stale rosters and directories reduce match and delivery accuracy.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Establish minimum practices for recipient directory maintenance, attribution files, roster updates, endpoint maintenance, delivery confirmation, and standardized roster/attribution exchange.

detailed_positions.rationale: Send rate alone does not show whether notifications reached authorized recipients or were timely/actionable.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Adopt objective measures for send rate, confirmed delivery rate, timeliness, recipient breadth, and closed-loop acknowledgment, with graduated enforcement and technical assistance.

solicitation_responses.summary: Provides extensive responses to the electronic event notification RFI, including data elements, standards, TEFCA, CoPs, directories, patient matching, attribution, measurement, and incentives.
Discusses FHIR Subscriptions, Da Vinci Unsolicited Notifications, endpoint/directory modernization, and automated discovery as future-state mechanisms but cautions against premature mandates.

recommendations: Recognize real-time event notifications as foundational care coordination services.
Preserve HL7 v2 ADT as the current production-ready real-time push standard.
Advance FHIR through phased pilots rather than broad premature mandates.
Ensure TEFCA evolves to support real-time push-based workflows.
Improve patient matching, attribution data, provider directories, roster standards, and endpoint maintenance.
Clarify permissible behavioral health and encounter-level sharing, including 42 CFR Part 2 issues.
Adopt tiered notification data profiles and avoid overburdening hospitals.
Create qualified notification arrangements and recognize technical routing vendors.
Measure send rate, confirmed delivery, timeliness, recipient breadth, and closed-loop acknowledgment.
Use outcome-based CoP requirements rather than prescribing a single technology before market readiness.

primary_concerns: Premature disruption of HL7 v2 ADT infrastructure.
TEFCA does not yet provide standardized real-time push event infrastructure.
No universally required production-ready FHIR ADT push specification exists today.
Patient matching, attribution, directories, and Part 2 uncertainty impede routing.
potential_negative_impacts_cited: Forced migration could impose cost, strain resource-limited hospitals, disrupt stable ADT feeds, and degrade real-time performance.
Suppression of behavioral health event data could delay interventions and increase readmission or adverse events.
implementation_barriers_mentioned: Fragmented HIE/vendor/network participation, variable standards implementation, custom onboarding, limited rural/CAH resources, EHR vendor readiness, legal/consent fragmentation, stale rosters.

supporting_evidence.data_or_statistics_cited: No formal statistics cited; provides operational observations about hospital supplemental fields and HL7 v2 ADT deployment.
supporting_evidence.studies_or_research_referenced: Recommends a national fill-rate study; no study results cited.
examples_provided: ADT event types A01, A03, A04, A08.
MLLP over VPN and HTTPS web services as common connectivity models.
Bamboo Health matching against customer rosters and delivering workflow-triggered notifications.

impact_assessment.economic_implications: Avoiding premature migration protects existing investment and prevents unnecessary re-engineering; better routing and automation may reduce downstream care coordination costs.
impact_assessment.technical_feasibility: Current HL7 v2 ADT workflows are feasible and mature; FHIR push models require pilots, conformance tools, and broader deployment before mandates.
impact_assessment.patient_care_impact: Timely notifications support transitions, outreach, post-discharge care, behavioral health follow-up, and value-based care performance.

key_quotes: HL7 v2 ADT remains the only universally deployed, production-ready, push-based event standard nationwide.
FHIR does not yet provide a standardized, production-ready push model equivalent to HL7 v2 ADT.
TEFCA should complement, not displace, existing real-time notification capabilities.
The most effective strategies do more than deliver an alert; they route it to the right team and support timely action.
